Hedonist

/HEE-duh-nist/ - the stress falls on HEE · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Hedonist means one who believes pleasure should be the primary pursuit of humans.

Casio the cat lives as a shameless hedonist, migrating around the house all day to occupy whichever patch of sunlight is warmest.

Worked Example

Uncle Fen renounced the family's dawn-jog tradition on his fortieth birthday, declared himself a hedonist, moved his armchair to the sunniest window, and subscribed to three chocolate-of-the-month clubs.

A hedonist doesn't just enjoy pleasure — everyone does that. A hedonist promotes pleasure to life's organizing principle: choices, calendars, and budgets all answer to it. The word can be a philosophy-classroom term or a raised eyebrow, depending on who is saying it.

Antonyms

How Strong Is It? — fun-lover → bon vivant → hedonist

fun-lover vs. hedonist

fun-lover vs. hedonist: A fun-lover is milder than a hedonist: happy to take pleasure when it arrives, never reorganizing life around it.

bon vivant vs. hedonist

bon vivant vs. hedonist: A bon vivant savors good living — fine tables, good company — but stops short of the hedonist's full creed that pleasure is the point of everything.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — hedon

Root — hedon: pleasure (Greek hēdonē)

Suffix — -ist

Suffix — -ist: one who believes in or practices

Put it together

Put it together: Hedon- (pleasure) + -ist (one who believes in it) = a believer in pleasure. Greek hēdonē named delight itself; ancient philosophers argued over whether it was life's true goal, and the people who answered yes have been hedonists ever since. The same root builds hedonism, the doctrine they signed up for.

Use the root in a new word: hedonism

Use the root in a new word: hedonism: The travel brochure promises a weekend of pure hedonism: hot springs, hammocks, and a dessert cart that never leaves the pool deck.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / often wry

Hedonist is the label for someone whose compass points at pleasure — as philosophy or lifestyle. A sybarite luxuriates, a glutton overeats, an epicure savors selectively; the hedonist outranks them all, because for him pleasure isn't a hobby but the whole point. His opposite number, the ascetic, renounces exactly what he enshrines.
